comments.text: CPU on-chip port data-direction register, initialized to $2F by the engine. The banking control bits in register $01 are outputs under this setup.
CPU on-chip port data register, normally $35 during gameplay, selecting RAM under the ROMs while retaining I/O access. Auxiliary graphics copies temporarily select $34 to reach RAM under I/O.
Horizontal fine-scroll phase, normally recentred to three. The camera controls update it when the viewport moves and the raster setup uses the corresponding display control value.
Vertical fine-scroll phase, normally recentred to four. The camera controls update it and detect character-row boundaries when it wraps past the three-bit range.
Nonzero keeps the current camera direction active. Recentring and map-boundary paths clear it before restoring the default fine-scroll state.
Zero means no selected displacement; one through eight select axial/diagonal camera control and transient-object offset tables.

Player horizontal screen coordinate in half-pixel units. $104A doubles it for sprites 0-2 and carries the ninth bit into $D010; the movement routines increment or decrement it after checking tile properties.
Player vertical coordinate used by the standing and wheel sprite layouts. The control routine changes it for falling and jumping and derives the terrain-row pointer from it.
Little-endian pointer into the current terrain screen used by movement collision checks. Its row comes from the split tables at $BF91/$BFAA; byte $D3 supplies the screen's high bank bits.
Column derived from (player_x_half_pixels minus $0C) divided by four. Movement tests use it with the tile-row pointer and offsets for the player's occupied cells.
Player upward-motion flag. The control routine sets it during the upward portion of a jump and clears it when the upward phase ends or the ceiling test blocks it.
Facing/direction value used by the horizontal controls: zero selects left, one right. Wheel collision with a wall also changes it to bounce in the opposite direction.
Index into the vertical movement table at $08F7. Jump ascent, ceiling collision and falling paths set or advance this value.
First sprite-shape number for the player's current animation. Standing form uses three consecutive shapes, while wheel form uses two and a fixed third pointer.

Nonzero selects the wheel's sprite layout, reduced collision height, faster horizontal step and wheel-specific animation. Down plus the CIA1 port-B bit-4 key test activates it; jumping with free space beneath can clear it.
Eleven actor type/status bytes indexed by slot X. Zero skips the slot, negative values take $579A and positive values dispatch through $08AE/$08BE.
Eleven actor horizontal coordinates in half-pixel units, indexed by slot. The multiplexing handler doubles the selected coordinate into the hardware sprite's X register and high bit.
Eleven actor vertical coordinates. The scroll compensation in $0CF4 adjusts these for active slots and the multiplexing routines select which slots occupy sprites 3-7.
Eleven sprite-shape numbers indexed by actor slot; copied into both screen buffers' sprite-pointer tables when a slot is selected for display.
Eleven actor colours indexed by slot, copied into the hardware sprite colour register by the multiplexing handler.
VIC memory-pointer value whose $10 bit selects between the $C800 and $CC00 character screens in video bank $C000. The scroll scheduler toggles this bit when exchanging buffers.
CPU high address byte for the active terrain character screen, toggled between $C8 and $CC. Terrain drawing combines it with row-offset high bytes to form screen pointers.
Nonzero enables the outward-moving terrain-cell wave update at $306F. Space activation writes $D3 here; the wave routine clears it once both fronts have left the screen.
Set when the main raster handler sees CIA1 port B bit 2 low. While set, it advances sound but bypasses gameplay until joystick fire is read low, which clears the flag.
Main-thread dispatch index. The table at $0A5B/$0A62 selects a busy wait, restart paths, the disk transition or the alternate start path; raster handlers request those transitions.
Message selector in the low bits, with bit seven requesting initial setup. Zero selects TIME OUT!, one GAME OVER and two CONTINUE?.
Zero-based position in the level progression. The transition at $544A increments it; $0B selects the ending path after the named file has loaded.
Two filename characters passed in X and Y to the fast loader at $6990. The level transition copies the next name from $8FEC/$8FED.
Countdown prescaler. The raster handler decrements it and reloads $32 when it reaches zero, then subtracts one from the three decimal digits at $080F-$0811.

Seventy-three eight-byte status-panel glyphs corresponding to character codes $80-$C8 with character base zero. They include border and icon pieces, TIME, compact timer digits, two-row decimal digits and the energy-bar fill states. This authored font occupies otherwise unused screen RAM, not the visible panel cells at $0748.
Five eight-byte glyphs at codes $90-$94 draw the TIME label and its punctuation in the status panel.
Ten eight-byte glyphs, codes $A2-$AB, draw timer digits zero through nine. $4BCE adds $A2 to each numeric time digit.
Ten glyphs, codes $AC-$B5, hold the upper halves of decimal digits for the score, lives and ammunition fields. The panel drawing routines add $AC to each BCD nibble.
Ten glyphs, codes $B6-$BF, hold the lower halves of the panel's decimal digits. They pair with the upper halves at $0560.
Address base used with screen character codes $80-$C8 to read the panel colour palette at $0648-$0690. The bytes at this base itself belong to the panel font, not the palette.
Continuation of the panel character bitmaps beginning at $0400. These rows include the energy-bar glyphs at the high end of the panel alphabet.
Five eight-byte glyphs at codes $C4-$C8 represent energy-cell fill levels. Refill advances the glyph toward $C8; damage reduces it toward $C4 and then moves to the preceding cell.
Seventy-three colour values corresponding to panel glyph codes $80-$C8. $6126 indexes these through base $05C8 plus the screen code, then writes them into the panel's colour RAM.
Eight delay-loop counts indexed by the fine vertical scroll bits in the panel-transition IRQ at $0C89. They align the display-mode change with the scrolling playfield.
Final four entries of the eight-count raster-delay table beginning at $0691. The raster alignment code selects the count from the low three raster bits.

Fifty-six damage bytes indexed by the screen character minus the collision cutoff at $F0, normally $C8. The collision probe returns that index in $C3 with carry set; level actor handlers subtract the selected value from health. Surround-flash setup temporarily sets the eighteen entries at $06AE-$06BF to two, then restores them when its records finish.

Damage entries beginning at character $DD, indexed by character minus $C8 through the table base $0699. The flash saves eighteen entries here, temporarily replaces them with two, and restores them when its records finish.
Indirect target used by the common IRQ entry at $0A2F. Raster handlers replace this pointer to schedule the next screen band.
Indirect return continuation used by $0C86 after the player-update portion of the raster handler. Initialized and replaced with the level's scheduling configuration.
Indirect continuation taken at $0C7A when $0819 requests a screen update. The request flag is cleared before dispatch.
Indirect continuation after $0C89 has selected the status-panel bank, screen and colours. Its target can return through the common interrupt exit.
Low and high address bytes copied into the raster-handler pointer by $0A74 when the next multiplexed sprite does not fall beyond its line limit.
JMP entry for the level-selected player controller. The normal platform levels select $1063; the flying levels replace its operand with their own controller.
Low target byte of the player JMP hook at $06DB. Stores to this address change the selected handler without adding another routine.
High target byte of the player JMP hook at $06DB. Stores to this address change the selected handler without adding another routine.
JMP entry used after player control to update the camera. Its normal target is $13E3; a level can redirect it, including to the return stub.
Low target byte of the camera JMP hook at $06DE. Stores to this address change the selected handler without adding another routine.
High target byte of the camera JMP hook at $06DE. Stores to this address change the selected handler without adding another routine.
JMP entry selecting the resident damage routine at $4C0C in the saved platform-game state.
JMP entry selecting the packed-decimal pending-score accumulator at $4AF9 in this state.
Load X through a self-modified immediate operand and jump to $0EA7, where the actor-dispatch loop decrements X and continues to the next slot.
Immediate slot operand of the LDX at $06E7. Actor dispatch patches it before jumping into a behavior so that the behavior can continue the descending slot loop.
Single RTS used as an empty target for level-selectable hooks.
JMP hook called instead of ordinary actor setup when $03E1 is nonzero. Its saved target is the return stub; level initialization can replace the operand.
Low target byte of the alternate player JMP hook at $06ED. Stores to this address change the selected handler without adding another routine.
High target byte of the alternate player JMP hook at $06ED. Stores to this address change the selected handler without adding another routine.
JMP hook selected in alternate display/update paths when $03E1 is nonzero. Its default target is the return stub.
Low target byte of the alternate update JMP hook at $06F0. Stores to this address change the selected handler without adding another routine.
High target byte of the alternate update JMP hook at $06F0. Stores to this address change the selected handler without adding another routine.
JMP hook called by the main actor-band IRQ before programming hardware sprites. The normal saved target is the playfield setup at $495C.
Low target byte of the playfield JMP hook at $06F3. Stores to this address change the selected handler without adding another routine.
High target byte of the playfield JMP hook at $06F3. Stores to this address change the selected handler without adding another routine.
JMP hook entered by energy depletion and timer-expiry paths. Its saved target is $4C4D.
JMP hook for the resident character-cell projectile updater at $3281 in the normal saved state.
Low target byte of the scatter update JMP hook at $06F9. Stores to this address change the selected handler without adding another routine.
High target byte of the scatter update JMP hook at $06F9. Stores to this address change the selected handler without adding another routine.
JMP hook called after the character-projectile updater when $07F2 is zero. Its saved target is $3623.
Low target byte of the laser update JMP hook at $06FC. Stores to this address change the selected handler without adding another routine.
High target byte of the laser update JMP hook at $06FC. Stores to this address change the selected handler without adding another routine.
JMP hook called in the gameplay update after projectile processing; its saved target is $44A2.
Low target byte of the bounce update JMP hook at $06FF. Stores to this address change the selected handler without adding another routine.
High target byte of the bounce update JMP hook at $06FF. Stores to this address change the selected handler without adding another routine.
JMP hook used by a newly pressed fire-button path when the player is not in wheel form. Its saved target is $3182, which allocates the normal weapon's character-cell projectiles.
Low target byte of the normal fire JMP hook at $0702. Stores to this address change the selected handler without adding another routine.
High target byte of the normal fire JMP hook at $0702. Stores to this address change the selected handler without adding another routine.
JMP wrapper for the exposed-row renderer at $2AE2.
JMP wrapper for the exposed-column renderer at $2BAA.
JMP wrapper for the vertical phase/pointer update at $2B46.
JMP wrapper for the reverse vertical phase/pointer update at $2B75.
JMP wrapper for the horizontal phase/pointer update at $2C0D.
JMP wrapper for the reverse horizontal phase/pointer update at $2C25.

Fifteen saved handler addresses: initial playfield IRQ, actor multiplexer, panel IRQ, camera, player, death, message, playfield rendering, selected/default scatter fire, laser fire, bounce fire and the three projectile update entries. Reset and level callbacks copy the required addresses into the mutable JMP hooks.
Saved $568F entry used to restore the actor sprite multiplexer through the raster hook.
High byte of the saved multiplexer address at $0719. This address is inside the saved word, not an instruction entry.
Low byte of the saved status-panel IRQ address at $071B/$071C, restored when the boss raster sequence finishes.
High byte of the saved status-panel IRQ address at $071B/$071C, paired with its low byte for the restore to $06D1/$06D2.
Saved camera entry $13E3; level callbacks can replace the live camera hook while retaining this default.
High byte of the saved camera address at $071D, used as part of that word.
Low byte of the saved playfield pointer at $0725, in the reset handler template beginning at $0717.
High byte of the saved playfield pointer at $0725, in the reset handler template beginning at $0717.
Low byte of the saved selected fire pointer at $0727, in the reset handler template beginning at $0717.
High byte of the saved selected fire pointer at $0727, in the reset handler template beginning at $0717.
Low byte of the saved scatter fire pointer at $0729, in the reset handler template beginning at $0717.
High byte of the saved scatter fire address at $0729. The scatter pickup copies the pair back into the normal-fire hook.
Low byte of the saved scatter update pointer at $072F, in the reset handler template beginning at $0717.
High byte of the saved scatter update pointer at $072F, in the reset handler template beginning at $0717.
Low byte of the saved laser update pointer at $0731, used when resetting the live projectile hook.
High byte of the saved laser update pointer at $0731, used when resetting the live projectile hook.
Low byte of the saved bounce update pointer at $0733, used when resetting the live projectile hook.
High byte of the saved bounce update pointer at $0733, used when resetting the live projectile hook.
Reload value for the damage-rate divider $EF. The damage routine reloads it when applying one energy step, and machine initialization installs one.
Next raster compare line installed by the actor/gameplay IRQ before enabling interrupts. Machine initialization selects $2A; level code can replace it.
Packed-decimal collected-diamond count. The pending-diamond path increments it, resets it at $50 and can award one continue through the nibble at $DBFF.
Packed-decimal ammunition counter initialized to three. The Space activation path at $2FBF-$2FCB refuses zero, decrements it with the BCD counter routine and redraws its panel field.
Once-per-life availability flag. Player reset sets it to one; the held-flash path requires it nonzero before super-weapon activation, and activation clears it.
Nonzero suppresses ordinary movement/damage paths while the super weapon controls the player. The special update clears it after restoring the saved state.
First of the four resident status-panel screen rows, including the static border and energy-bar surround. Generated energy cells within this row are excluded from authored-data coverage.
Authored panel cell forming the energy bar right border; adjacent numeric or energy cells are generated separately.

Status-panel row containing the static icons and upper digit surroundings for lives, continues, diamonds and power lines; score upper halves occupy its right edge. Digit cells are generated by $4B0F-$4BBD.
Authored panel cell forming the separator after the life upper digits; adjacent numeric or energy cells are generated separately.
Generated upper half of the continue count, drawn from the low nibble of $DBFF by $4BBD.
12 authored panel decoration cells between continue and diamond counters. These retain the panel template while adjacent counters are redrawn.
5 authored panel decoration cells between diamond and power-line counters. These retain the panel template while adjacent counters are redrawn.
2 authored panel decoration cells between power-line and score counters. These retain the panel template while adjacent counters are redrawn.
Authored panel cell forming the right edge after the score upper digits; adjacent numeric or energy cells are generated separately.
Third panel row, with static decorations around the lower digit halves and the three compact time digits. The score's lower halves are drawn at $07B8-$07BE.
Authored panel cell forming the separator after the life lower digits; adjacent numeric or energy cells are generated separately.
3 authored panel decoration cells between the continue lower half and compact time digits. These retain the panel template while adjacent counters are redrawn.
Three generated single-height time digits written by $4BCE from the hundreds, tens and units at $0811-$080F.
6 authored panel decoration cells between time and diamond lower halves. These retain the panel template while adjacent counters are redrawn.
5 authored panel decoration cells between diamond and power-line lower halves. These retain the panel template while adjacent counters are redrawn.
2 authored panel decoration cells between power-line and score lower halves. These retain the panel template while adjacent counters are redrawn.
Seven generated lower-half score glyphs written by $4B0F. Static panel decoration continues after these digit cells through the following row.
Static border cell immediately following the seven lower score digits. It joins the authored bottom-panel decoration at $07C0.
Forty authored screen cells forming the status panel's bottom decoration; the font is the resident panel alphabet at $0400.

Selector for the normal shot allocation paths: zero takes the single-projectile path, one the three-record groups and other values the five-record groups. The super weapon saves it, selects two and restores it afterward.
Selector into the six laser configuration groups through $37B5. The super weapon saves it, selects five and restores it afterward.
Bounce-weapon upgrade selector. Zero omits the split-on-impact path, nonzero permits allocating fragments, and value two enables axis-reflection tests before the projectile's next cell is drawn.
Surround-flash activity/count byte, recomputed by walking the twenty beam slots. Several ordinary projectile and player paths are gated while it is nonzero.
Maximum beam-record travel count tested against $030D+slot in the surround-flash updater. Machine initialization sets it to $10; upgrades and resets can replace it.

Fire-hold counter. A fresh press stores zero; successive eligible held updates increment it until $13, when surround-flash setup begins. At $13, subsequent held calls use the active aiming/emission path.
Four packed-decimal award bytes accumulated into the score by $4AF9 and cleared by that addition.
Four packed-decimal score bytes, most significant first. $4AF9 adds the pending award in reverse byte order and $4B0F displays seven digits.

Least significant decimal digit of the remaining level time. Borrow underflow reloads this digit to nine and decrements $0810, then $0811. Reaching the end requests the expiry hook and increments $03E5.
Middle decimal digit of the remaining time, decremented when the units digit underflows and reset to nine when borrowing from $0811.
Most significant decimal digit of the remaining time. A negative borrow invokes the expiry path, as does finding all three digits zero at the start of a countdown update.

Eight split low/high entry addresses for the axial and diagonal camera controls at $1496, $14FF, $1564, $15FB, $1685, $1728, $17CE and $1879. The direction selector indexes them with values one through eight using bases one byte earlier.
High-byte lookup base for scroll direction indices one through eight. Effective entries are $082A-$0831, paired with low bytes read through base $0821.
Eight split addresses for in-place colour-RAM shifts, selected by the direction index in $1924.
High-byte half of the eight colour-buffer shift pointers at $0832, selected by the scroll direction.

Sixteen split addresses for the character-buffer scroll copies: eight directions for one source/destination buffer selection followed by eight for the opposite selection. $1924 chooses the half after toggling the screen-selection bit.
High-byte half of the sixteen character-buffer copy pointers beginning at $0842. The first eight select one buffer direction and the second eight select the other buffer.
Half-pixel X threshold tested by the rightward camera control when the fine-scroll phase reaches its centred position.
Half-pixel X threshold tested by the camera selector to request a rightward or right-diagonal scroll.
Base used with direction indices zero through eight for projectile restoration coordinates. Direction zero has no shift; the eight directional entries are $0865-$086C.

Eight signed character-column adjustments for directions one through eight. The coordinate-correction loop indexes them with direction minus one; restoration paths index the preceding base $0864 with the direction itself.
Direction-three entry within the column-step table at $0865. Player reset installs minus one here, while movement can replace associated scroll-step entries.
Base used with direction indices zero through eight for projectile restoration rows. Direction zero has no shift; directional entries follow at $086E-$0875.
Eight signed row adjustments paired with the column steps at $0865. The correction loop indexes by direction minus one, while restoration paths use base $086D with the direction itself.
Base used with direction indices one through eight to read half-pixel actor X corrections at $0876-$087D. This base byte also completes the preceding row-step table.
Eight half-pixel X-coordinate corrections selected by directions one through eight through base $0875. The player movement path can replace the entry at $0879 to match its horizontal movement step.
Direction-three actor X correction. The player movement path writes its positive horizontal step here; the paired negative step is stored at $0879.
Direction-four X correction within the actor-scroll table. The player movement path writes its negated horizontal step here; reset restores minus one.
Address base used with direction indices one through eight to read the actor pixel-Y corrections at $087E-$0885. The byte at the base itself is the final X-correction entry.
Eleven offscreen Y values, copied to actor Y on reset and by actor-release paths. The ascending actor slot chooses successively smaller negative-byte coordinates.

Seven colour values selected by the explosion animation index. $579A advances the index, selects this colour and adds the index to the sprite base at $0898; index seven releases the actor instead of reading another colour.
First sprite number for the seven-frame actor explosion. The updater adds its animation index to this value and chooses the paired colour from $0891.
Initial closed-orb sprite pointer selected by the resident orb handler; reset writes $90 into this byte. The shape was rendered from the gameplay sprite bank.
Sprite number selected when actor type sixteen initializes a projectile. The resident projectile handler copies it into that actor slot's sprite pointer.
Ten sprite pointers indexed by collectible subtype. The first six share an orb shape and differ by colour; energy, ammunition, life and diamond use their own shapes.
Ten colours paired with the subtype sprite pointers at $089B. These distinguish the six reward orbs sharing a shape.

Seventeen low-byte entries indexed by actor type zero through sixteen. The high-byte table begins at $08BE, overlapping the final low byte: both stored values are $27. Type zero is skipped; type sixteen combines $27 with $5B at $08CE to reach the projectile handler $5B27.

Shared byte $27: low byte of actor handler sixteen and high byte of reserved handler zero. The seventeen high-byte entries continue through $08CE. A six-instruction live dispatch trace confirmed type sixteen reaches $5B27.
Last high byte in the overlapping seventeen-entry actor directory, giving type sixteen its $5B27 projectile handler.
Four offsets, twelve/eight/four/zero, selected by the vertical sub-block phase when reading a four-by-four terrain block definition. Row and column drawing paths share this reversed row order.
Seven sprite numbers selected by the descending walk-animation index for facing left. The right-facing sequence begins at $08DA.
Seven right-facing walk-animation sprite numbers, paired with the left-facing sequence at $08D3. $095B selects one sequence through the facing flag.
Two facing-dependent player sprite numbers selected by the Down-control path. The same pair supplies the crouched pose when a flash is fired from that posture.
Two facing-dependent standing sprite numbers used by ordinary player movement, the flash setup and super-weapon restoration.
Two facing-dependent airborne sprite numbers selected while the jump/fall path updates the player's Y coordinate.
Colour assigned to both multicolour player sprites in the standing renderer. Level code can replace this palette byte.
Colour used by the standing player's outline sprite and the first wheel sprite. Player reset and level callbacks can replace it.
Lower player-Y bound tested by the fire-processing gate before a weapon can be emitted. Initialization installs $32.
Upper player-Y bound tested by the fire-processing gate. Initialization installs $B6.
Mutable vertical alignment subtracted from standing sprite Y. The player controller selects two when the vertical fine-scroll phase is four.
Eleven signed Y adjustments indexed by the wheel transition counter $03DE. The wheel movement path applies them while the cell below is passable, then increments the counter toward ten.

Forty-two vertical displacements indexed by the jump counter. Early positive entries raise the player, zero entries hold the crest, and the final negative bytes move down; the movement paths subtract the selected byte from player Y.
Two signed horizontal adjustments selected by facing and added to the player's half-pixel X in the walking-animation routine.
Three runtime animation indices for the flashing player's three hardware-sprite components, each cycling through the six-shape table at $0931.
Three runtime countdowns paired with $0923. Each reloads to three when advancing its component's animation index.
Standing/wheel offset pair added to the first two flashing-player sprite Y positions through base $0929. The third component uses the next pair at $092B; the colours begin separately at $092D.
Pair of standing/wheel offsets used for the third hardware sprite, within the component-offset data beginning at $0929.
Four colours selected by the low two CIA timer bits during the final part of the invulnerability countdown. Earlier phases use the active effect colour directly.
Six sprite numbers for the wheel's rotating body. $0F83 places the chosen shape in both screen-buffer sprite directories.
Eight loop-delay counts indexed by the raster line's low three bits at $0CF4. They align the panel-to-game display-control write; this is timing data, not sprite colour data.
Search actor slots ten down to zero for a zero type byte. Return Y as the free index, or with its negative flag set after all eleven slots are occupied.
Restore the slot's hidden Y coordinate from $0886 and clear its type, format and X coordinate, then return to the actor loop through $06E7.

Advance the seven-frame walking animation when its divider expires, choosing the left/right shape sequence from $08DA/$08D3. Add the facing-indexed horizontal step at $0921 to the player X coordinate; crossing $A8 enters the viewport/transition mask setup at $098E.
Clear the mask sense byte $77, set the transition flag $07FE to one and reset its sequence cursor $78. The raster chain then updates the mask using $49EA.

Fill the first page of the other screen buffer and eight mask accumulators with $FF, select the inverse mask sense, set $07FE and reset its cursor. The mask completion path selects a main-thread transition stage.
High address byte of the STA at $0998, patched from the active buffer page XOR four. The loop clears one page of the other screen buffer during the viewport transition.

Test actor slot X against a player-relative rectangle using the two supplied extents in A and Y and the player's animation offset $1D. The compare/subtract sequence preserves carry between steps; return carry set for an accepted overlap and clear on the rejection exits.
Immediate extent in the ADC at $09C0, part of the overlap probe's vertical upper-bound calculation. The dimensions passed in A/Y are kept separately in $DF/$DD.
Immediate extent in the ADC at $09D2, part of the overlap probe's final horizontal upper-bound calculation. This label names an operand, not another collision routine.

Reject actor positions outside the playfield, convert its screen position to a terrain row pointer and column, and inspect a two-by-two group of character cells. A character at or above the cutoff in $F0 returns its relative index in $C3, replaces the hit cell with $FF and returns carry set. Otherwise return carry clear. The level's actor behavior uses the index to look up damage.
Preserve A, X and Y on the stack, acknowledge the VIC interrupt with DEC $D019, then dispatch through $06D1. The handler's continuation restores the registers at $0A3A.
Restore Y, X and A saved by the IRQ entry and return with RTI. The byte at $0A3F is also the NMI return instruction.
Little-endian ending return vector $53E4. The ending exits through JMP ($0A40) at $7C9E; a targeted instruction step confirmed that it enters the resident title-file loader handler.
Disable interrupts, reset the stack and call the machine setup at $5003, then enter the main-thread stage dispatcher.

Read $03E4, copy the corresponding low and high target bytes from $0A5B/$0A62 into the JMP operand at $0A59/$0A5A, and jump there. Stage zero selects this same busy-wait entry; interrupt code supplies other stages.
Low target byte of the main-stage dispatch JMP at $0A58. It is an operand inside that dispatcher, not a separate routine.
High target byte of the main-stage dispatch JMP at $0A58. It is an operand inside that dispatcher, not a separate routine.
Seven low bytes for the main-thread dispatch targets, paired with the high bytes at $0A62. Stage zero waits at $0A49; stage four enters the level transition at $544A.
Seven high bytes paired with $0A5B. Together they name $0A49, $53C6, $53DE, $53E4, $544A, $5563 and $5571.
Wait until the raster high bit is set, then write $6C to the VIC control register through its $D151 mirror. The disk-transition paths use this to change the display outside the playfield.

Enable sprites, call the level's $06F3 hook and schedule the next raster band. Copy selected actor positions, multicolour flags, colours and shape pointers into hardware sprites 3-7 and both screen pointer tables. Handle pause, the countdown divider and player-update gates, then dispatch to the selected raster continuation.

Delay according to the current fine vertical scroll, clear sprite expansion and horizontal positions, select extended-colour text and schedule $0CF4. Switch the VIC to bank zero and screen $0400, set the panel's background colours and scroll control, then jump through $06D7.

Align the panel display transition, install the next IRQ handler and update active actor coordinates by the scroll offsets in $0875/$087D when permitted. Dispatch active actors through the split behavior table $08AE/$08BE, then update collisions, weapons, rewards and sound through the resident and level hooks before returning from the IRQ.

Read each of eleven actor types in descending slot order. Zero skips a slot, negative types enter the explosion updater, and positive types select a handler through the split table at $08AE/$08BE. Patch the loop-return hook with the current slot before jumping.
Low operand byte of the JMP at $0EA4, replaced from $08AE indexed by the active actor type. It belongs to the actor-dispatch instruction, not a separate routine.

High operand byte of the actor-dispatch JMP at $0EA4, replaced from $08BE. After each selected behavior returns through the actor-loop hook, the enclosing IRQ continues with projectiles, rewards and sound before restoring the saved registers.

Draw sprites 0-2 from the player position and shape number unless $0812 suppresses drawing. $0815 selects a blinking three-sprite effect with its own shape sequence and colour cycle; otherwise choose standing or wheel geometry, colours and multicolour flags. Finish by doubling the player X coordinate and updating the three high-X bits together.

Derive terrain row and column pointers and collision height for standing or wheel form. Draw 21 characters down the destination column supplied in A/X. Increment the horizontal sub-block phase at $08; wrapping from three to zero increments both map pointers at $02/$03 and $04/$05 by one map byte.
Decrement the horizontal sub-block phase at $08; underflow wraps it to three and decrements both map pointers by one map byte.

Starting from the saved map pointer and vertical sub-block phase, draw ten block columns across 21 character rows into the selected screen and colour RAM. Refuse fire processing in blocked player states or outside the permitted playfield coordinate range, then read joystick port-two fire through $DC00 bit four. A fresh press records the button state and either starts the selected normal weapon through $0702 or takes the wheel-specific path; a held press jumps to the held-fire handler at $3931.

Find a free entry among four bomb slots. Use the held joystick direction to select a placement offset relative to the player's tile position, mark the slot new, set its twelve-stage/four-update timer and request effect $1B. No ammunition counter is consumed by this allocation path.

Update four character-cell bomb records. A new record saves its terrain character and draws glyph $DD with colour nine. Timed updates blink the colour and, on expiry, restore the saved cell in both screen buffers, activate matching bonus-block terrain and allocate a sprite effect when a slot is available. A short player-animation disturbance uses CIA timer samples and later restores the saved animation state.
Six joystick masks searched from index five down toward zero when placing a wheel bomb. A zero result from AND with $DC00 selects the corresponding signed column and row offsets.
Six signed player-relative bomb-column offsets, paired with the direction-mask search at $2F83.
Six player-relative bomb-row offsets paired with the column offsets at $2F89.

Return carry set on activation and clear on refusal.

If $017E is active, restore saved character and colour cells behind two horizontal wave fronts, move the fronts outward and draw $EF/$F0 into passable cells. Mark blocked rows, save the cells each front overwrites and animate the two wave character patterns at $C778/$C780 using CIA timer samples. Clear the active flag when both fronts have left the screen.

Walk five laser records. Angle 29 has 3 phases. Its parallel glyph, companion offset, horizontal step and vertical step arrays occupy $4020-$402B; phase advances modulo 3 in $3A37.
Angle 30 has 2 phases. Its parallel glyph, companion offset, horizontal step and vertical step arrays occupy $402C-$4033; phase advances modulo 2 in $3A37.
Angle 31 has 4 phases. Its parallel glyph, companion offset, horizontal step and vertical step arrays occupy $4034-$4043; phase advances modulo 4 in $3A37.
Fifty-nine eight-byte monochrome glyph fragments. The angle copy programs read contiguous groups here into the mutable flash glyph area; commands with bit seven set reverse the source-byte order.

Twenty damage bytes restored to $06AE-$06C1 by $51B8, covering the bomb, laser, scatter and two power-line characters. The eighteen entries through $06BF are also temporarily replaced during the flash.

On a new request, save the level's three playfield colours and request three sound effects. Walk the twelve-entry colour sequences at $428D/$4299/$42A5, then restore the saved colours and clear the request.
Twelve values for the first playfield colour during the special palette flash; the updater indexes them in descending order.
Twelve values paired with $428D for the second playfield colour.
Twelve values paired with the other two colour sequences for the third playfield colour.

Refuse an already active special weapon. Save position, facing and the three normal-weapon selectors; select their high-power values, enter wheel geometry and set the special flag. Consume the once-per-life availability flag at $0739, initialize its movement and lifetime state, and select the wheel shape. The held-flash caller checks availability before entering here.

Wait for existing surround-flash records to finish, then decrement the special lifetime. During the effect keep resetting the level-time divider, move the player around screen bounds with CIA-timer-selected direction changes and terrain reflection, animate wheel shapes, and emit bombs plus the three normal weapon families. At expiry restore the saved position, facing and weapon selectors, clear special/wheel/held-fire state and request a palette flash.
Eighteen colour values cycled by the panel IRQ through $0741 while the once-per-life super weapon is available. The selected value colours the two panel cells at $DB71/$DB72.

Find a free primary record among slots zero through two, seed its direction and terrain-grid position from the player, mark it $D3 and request effect four. Reject a starting row beyond the permitted screen area.

Walk nine bounce-projectile records, restoring their old terrain cells and colours before movement. Primary type three uses four glyphs in a two-by-two shape; split type two uses a single cell. The upgrade at $07F0 controls splitting and axis reflection on terrain. Clip to the screen, activate bonus-block terrain through $488C/$3827, and mirror changed cells into the second screen buffer when visible.

Immediate operand at $4688, patched from the previous top-left projectile cell at $4602-$4604. The enclosing bounce updater uses its $FF test when deciding whether a four-cell projectile can continue, then advances, redraws, collides or frees the slot. This byte is part of an instruction rather than an independent routine.
Two signed starting-column offsets, minus one and plus two, indexed by player facing when allocating a primary bounce shot.
Two signed offsets, plus two and minus two, used when allocating the paired fragments after a bounce-shot impact.
Search the eight character codes at $489A for A, from the final entry toward the first. Return carry set and Y as the matching quadrant/type index, or carry clear when no component matches.
Eight terrain character codes recognized by $488C as components of a bonus block. Their matching X/Y correction tables are at $48A2/$48AA.
Eight column corrections, indexed by the component match, subtracted from the hit position to find the block's top-left cell.
Eight row corrections paired with $48A2 for locating the impacted bonus block.

Select the other screen buffer's sprite-pattern base and schedule the sprite-row IRQ at $4987. Update the transition mask through $49EA. For an active mask, distribute seven expanded black sprites across the top, prepare their pointer-table stores and schedule successive rows; on completion reset the player and return to the normal panel schedule.

Combine the horizontal and vertical fine phases with the display-control bits, select the character screen through $D2, choose VIC bank $C000 and load the level's three playfield colours from $8FD0-$8FD2.

Write one shape pointer into seven sprite-pointer cells, advance the shape cursor and move the seven sprites down by $2A lines. After four rows, switch to the panel handler and restore its delay count; otherwise schedule the next row's raster line.
Immediate sprite-number operand at $4987. Transition setup selects the other buffer's sprite pool; the raster handler increments this operand after placing each sprite row.

Write the selected shape number to seven hardware-sprite directory cells, advance the cursor, and move their Y positions down by $2A. After four rows install the panel IRQ and its alignment delay; otherwise schedule the next row.

Unless the mask is idle or complete, select a position from the 64-byte order table at $4AB9 and set/clear its bit in one of eight mask bytes. Expand the resulting mask values into the other screen buffer's sprite patterns using offsets at $4A9E. At the final position, update the mask flag and request the appropriate main stage for level/death/continue handling.
Fill the first page of the other character-screen buffer and eight mask bytes with $FF. The target page is selected by a self-modified store operand derived from $D3 XOR four.
High destination byte of the STA at $4A90, patched to the other buffer page before filling that page and its mask bytes with $FF.

Eleven offsets separated by twenty-four bytes. The mask updater combines one with three times the selected mask-column index to write repeated three-byte strips into the other buffer's sprite patterns.
Eight ascending bit masks, $01 through $80. The transition order byte's high nibble selects one to set or clear in the active mask column.
Eight low-byte X coordinates for the expanded transition sprites. Setup subtracts its alignment offset before assigning each hardware sprite's X position.
Sixty-four packed positions determining the order in which the eight-by-eight transition mask changes. The low three bits select the mask column and the high nibble selects its bit.

In decimal mode, add the four packed-BCD pending-score bytes at $07F6-$07F9 to $07FA-$07FD, propagating carry from the last byte toward the first. Clear each pending byte as it is consumed, then fall through to draw the score.

Draw seven decimal digits from the four packed-BCD score bytes at $07FA-$07FD into two panel rows. Add glyph bases $AC and $B6 to each nibble, and restore X through a self-modified immediate operand before returning.
Immediate X operand in the LDX at $4B3E. Score drawing saves its caller's X here and restores it before returning.

Subtract one from the packed-decimal lives counter at $FFFC. A result without borrow jumps to the life display; a borrow falls through into the bounded life-award entry, whose comparison with $99 prevents adding to the wrapped value. Finish by drawing both BCD digits.
In decimal mode compare the lives byte with $99; values below that receive an ADC of one using the comparison's carry, then the resulting value is drawn. Values at or above $99 are drawn unchanged.
Clear decimal mode and draw both nibbles of the packed-BCD lives byte at $FFFC into the two-by-two component cells at $0775/$079D and $0776/$079E.

Increment the packed-BCD counter at $0737+X and draw it. A carry goes through the overflow path: a wrapped zero returns without drawing, while other values are decremented before drawing. X also selects the destination through $4BBB.
Load the packed-decimal counter at $0737+X. Zero returns; otherwise subtract one in decimal mode, store the result and fall through to draw that counter.
Draw the two BCD nibbles of $0737+X using top and bottom glyph bases $AC/$B6. The two-entry position table at $4BBB selects the panel field.
Two offsets, $15 and $1C, added to panel base $0770 by $4B95 for counters $0737 and $0738.
Mask the low nibble of the value kept at $DBFF and draw it at panel cells $0778 and $07A0 with the two component-glyph bases.
Draw the three numeric digits at $0811, $0810 and $080F into panel cells $07A4-$07A6 using the compact digit glyphs beginning at $A2.
Enable the energy-bar update flag, clear its cell cursor and fill seven panel cells at $0768-$076E with glyph $C4.
Advance one energy-bar cell's glyph toward $C8, moving the cursor right after a cell is full. Finishing the seventh cell clears the update flag; otherwise update the bar's colours through $4C3A.

Suppress damage while the refill, special-state or immunity flags are set. Otherwise decrement the damage delay, reload it from $0735 on expiry and reduce the current energy-bar cell. Move to the previous cell at its lower glyph limit; an empty first cell jumps to the death hook at $06F6. Recolour the bar after a change.
Use the current energy-cell index X to select a colour from $4C46 and apply it to the seven colour-RAM cells at $DB68-$DB6E.
Seven colours indexed by energy-bar cell position: $0A, $0A, $0F, $0F, $0B, $0D and $0D.

Select the normal death effects unless the level's mode bypasses them, seed sprite burst delays from CIA timer samples, save the player controller and replace it with $4CA8. Hide ordinary player drawing, mark the death state, downgrade weapon levels through $4DD7 and enter the life-loss hook at $4CA5.
JMP to the life-loss routine, normally $4B41. Resetting the projectile-damage template also restores this JMP operand.
Low target byte of the life loss JMP at $4CA5. It is an operand inside that dispatcher, not a separate routine.
High target byte of the life loss JMP at $4CA5. It is an operand inside that dispatcher, not a separate routine.

Update the three sprite-burst channels, or two in the selected alternate mode. Wait until the burst and fade counters finish, then hide the burst shapes and select timer-expiry, game-over, player reset or the inverse viewport-mask route according to the saved flags, mode and remaining lives.

Initialize one burst channel from CIA-timer-selected positions and timing, then alternate its hardware sprite between two positions. After its delay, walk the seven-entry shape/colour fade sequence. The shared burst counter controls reseeding; the channel eventually reaches a zero phase so death handling can finish.
Decrement each nonzero scatter, laser and bounce upgrade. Subtract four from the surround-flash length and replace a result below $10 with $10.
Seven sprite shape pointers used in reverse phase order by the death-burst channels.
Seven colours paired with the death-burst shape sequence.
Three hardware-sprite register offsets, zero, two and four, selecting sprites 0-2 for the burst channels.
Three masks that clear the selected sprite's X-high bit before its new doubled X value supplies the carry.
Three masks that set the selected sprite's X-high bit when its doubled X coordinate carries.
Three SID voice-register offsets selecting which effect-request byte receives the burst sound.

On a new high-bit request, configure three expanded hires sprites for TIME OUT!, GAME OVER or CONTINUE? and request the panel graphics through main stage two. Move the sprites into and out of view, hold them for the message timer, and route the final state to retry, continue selection or the viewport transition.

Animate the selected YES/NO highlight and read joystick left/right to change the choice when permitted. Fire accepts a valid displayed choice, ends the message hold and requests the corresponding sound. Choosing YES decrements the continue nibble at $DBFF and redraws it; flying-mode handling also calls its music command entry.
Toggle the YES-state flag on its divider and invert the selected bit patterns in the copied continue-message sprite data, using the message buffer pointer at $D9/$DA.
Toggle the NO-state flag on its divider and invert the corresponding bit patterns in the copied continue-message sprite data.

Copy 512 bytes from $5BC8 into the other screen buffer, using it as a pool of eight sprite patterns. Record a pointer-number offset for the selected buffer; the message pointer tables combine these shapes into three-sprite words.
High source byte of the LDA at $4FE7. The 512-byte message copy starts in page $5B and increments this byte for its second page.
High destination byte of the STA at $4FEA. The message copy selects the other character buffer and increments the page after each 256-byte pass.
Three shape pointers for the first sprite of TIME OUT!, GAME OVER and CONTINUE?, with the other two sprite selectors in the next two tables.
Three shape pointers for the middle message sprite, paired with $4FFA.
Three shape pointers for the final message sprite, paired with $4FFA/$4FFD.

Configure the processor port for RAM with I/O visible, blank the display and clear working state. Restore control and weapon hook operands from their saved defaults, initialize sound, displays, terrain, player and actors, set the first filename to 11 and level index to zero, then enable the game's raster interrupt schedule.

Wait for the high raster half, disable and acknowledge both CIA interrupt masks, enable the VIC raster source, select line $E6 and handler $48B2, acknowledge pending VIC status and enable CPU interrupts.

Default the three continuation pointers to the IRQ exit, install the hardware NMI and IRQ vectors and the first actor-band handler, and restore level hooks and timing defaults. Program CIA1 timer A, clear the level-provided workspace up to $BD91 and zero $FF80-$FFBF.
Clear fourteen entries in each of the arrays at $C4, $02A9, $0303, $0200, $026E and $0814. These are transient object and player-effect work areas rather than level-authored data.

Copy twenty damage values from $421C into $06AE-$06C1, corresponding to character codes $DD-$F0 with the normal collision cutoff $C8. Restore the operand at $4CA6/$4CA7 to the life-loss routine $4B41.
Set the two packed-decimal panel counters at $0737 and $0738 to zero and three respectively, drawing each through $4B95 with X selecting its panel position. Lives are a separate counter at $FFFC.
Set X to one and counter $0738 to three, then draw the ammunition field through $4B95.
Restore eleven saved bytes from $03F2 into $02-$0C, subtract the saved horizontal offset from the map position, adjust the saved player X coordinate and clear the offset before returning.

Initialize animation dividers and facing, clear jumping, wheel, pause and player-effect flags and sprite expansion/priority, then restore the player position from the checkpoint. If $03E5 requests a timer reset, reload its three digits from $8FE7-$8FE9. Restore the normal player shape and its control-hook address.
Clear eleven actor slots' X, type, format and movement-state arrays. Seed each slot's Y from $0886 and the sorting/index array from its slot number; set shared sprite multicolours to $0F and $0B.

Copy map position and scroll parameters from the level header at $8FC8-$8FDA into working state and save a checkpoint copy. Set the player start position and three timer digits, reset the timer divider, draw the timer and jump through the level initialization slot at $8FE1.

Zero the engine's zero page, lower stack/work pages and actor-state areas in four indexed passes, then clear $FF80-$FFFB and the work area beginning at $07E8. This is initialization output, not authored data to decode as tables.

Generate paired LDA/STA instruction sequences in $CB69 and $CF69 to copy successive colour values from $BFFF downward into the first and last cells of terrain rows. Append the 17-byte tail at $1B8B to both generated routines. The destination screen buffers therefore also hold executable scratch code outside the visible rows.
Write A to the generated code at $CB69+X and $CF69+X and increment X. The generator uses it for each opcode and source-operand byte.
Restore the scrolling checkpoint, reconstruct the terrain and colour-copy code, reset actors and transient slots, restore the player hooks and scroll state, then clear the main-stage request.
Call $4FCC and clear the main-stage request through $5584. The called routine determines the transition's player-visible meaning.

If flight music is active, request its transition and wait through the raster delay loop. Stop the engine, load the CD side-identity file and prompt until side one is inserted. Load title file 9% and jump to its entry at $7FF5.

Increment $03EF, retain the next filename from $8FEC/$8FED, blank and clear the playfield, and show the loading message. At index four require disk identity two. The $60F8 table decides whether to load an S-prefixed auxiliary file and copy its buffer under I/O. Load the level filename, invoke its setup hooks and return to the stage-zero wait; index $0B instead jumps to the ending at $7A01.
Restore three lives, select the current level filename from $8FEA/$8FEB and enter the common level-loading path at $5453.
Fill four 200-byte colour-RAM spans with colour nine, then clear the main-stage request and return to the main dispatcher.
Store zero to $03E4 and jump back to $0A49, leaving the main thread waiting for a request from the interrupt-driven engine.

Derive nearby 32-character grid coordinates from the map position and examine one of four neighbouring cells per call. Use the level row-offset and split-pointer tables at $8E64/$8E89/$8F11 to scan four-byte actor records. Allocate a free one of eleven slots when the record lies in the viewport, extract its type and subtype, clear its source type nibble, and initialize its sprite marker to $FE. Advance the neighbour selector modulo four.

Use the sorted actor index and current hardware-sprite offset to copy a slot's Y, doubled X, high-X bit, format, colour and shape pointer into sprites 3-7. Cycle the hardware sprite selection, advance the sorted slot and schedule another raster stop after the previous sprite's vertical span. Switch to the panel handler at $0C89 when the remaining actors fall past the permitted lines.
Five byte offsets select which of sprites 3-7 is reused next by the multiplexer.

Five interleaved AND/OR mask pairs for hardware sprites three through seven. The multiplexer indexes the clearing bytes with even register offsets and uses the adjacent setting byte through base $570B.
OR-mask base one byte after $570A. Even hardware-register offsets select the five setting masks, paired with the AND masks used for sprite X high bits and multicolour control.

Rebuild the actor Y-order linked list using eleven Y coordinates and the link array at $A6, then flatten it into the slot-index array at $B1. The multiplexer takes its initial hardware-sprite assignments from this ordered list.

Copy Y coordinates from the five initially selected actor slots to hardware sprites 3-7. Unless $03E0 supplies an alternate schedule, derive the next actor-band line from the last sprite's Y plus $16, with a lower limit of $39.

Initialize a newly marked negative-type actor as an explosion using the level-selected starting shape and a sound request. Thereafter advance its colour/shape sequence on a divider, releasing the slot after the final phase; return through the actor-loop hook after each update.

Initialize an orb's shape, colour, horizontal direction and movement phases, preserving its reward subtype in the low seven bits of $6F+slot. Bounce against terrain using the 50-entry vertical step curve. Player contact can inflict damage; wheel/immunity contact, a projectile character or the palette-effect flag converts it to collectible actor type two, requests a sound and adds a score award.
Fifty signed Y increments used cyclically by the bouncing orb. The actor's vertical phase decrements and wraps to the final entry; terrain contact selects a bounce phase.
Twenty-four colours indexed by the orb's independent animation phase.

On first update select the subtype's shape and colour and initialize movement timers. Subtypes below eight float upward on a divider; life/diamond subtypes follow a vertical curve with terrain checks. Remove out-of-range actors, test overlap with the player and dispatch the reward through the ten-entry handler table at $5B09/$5B13.
Low target byte of the pickup reward JMP at $5A35. It is an operand inside that dispatcher, not a separate routine.
High target byte of the pickup reward JMP at $5A35. It is an operand inside that dispatcher, not a separate routine.
Increase the scatter upgrade unless it equals two, select the saved normal-shot entry from $0729/$072A as the fire hook, record weapon selection zero and finish the pickup reward.
Increase the laser upgrade unless it equals five, install $35CD as the fire hook, record weapon selection one and finish the pickup reward.
Increase the bounce upgrade unless it equals two, install $4471 as the fire hook, record weapon selection two and finish the pickup reward.
Increase the surround-flash travel limit by two and clamp a result at or above $28 to $28, then enter the common pickup reward path.
Request the palette/actor effect through $07EB when idle and reset its palette cursor to eleven, then finish the common pickup reward.

Set effect flag $0815 and clear countdown/blink phase $0816/$0817, then finish the common pickup reward. On the first eligible decrement a zero countdown wraps to $FF; the drawing path clears the flag when a later decrement reaches zero. The alternating blink path gates those decrements.
Increment the energy-refill flag $1B and finish the common pickup reward.

Select counter $0738. If its BCD value equals $99, return through the actor loop without the ordinary pickup-removal path; otherwise increment and draw it before awarding the pickup score and releasing the actor.
Increment the pending diamond count at $61 and release the collectible actor. The gameplay IRQ consumes that pending count, awards its score and handles the fifty-diamond continue threshold.
Call the bounded packed-decimal life-award entry, then use the common pickup score/removal path.
Set the pending BCD award to 250 through $07F8/$07F9, accumulate/draw it, then release the current collectible actor.

Forty-five signed vertical increments indexed by $03D2+slot for the life and diamond movement path. Terrain checks replace or hold selected phases; the earlier pickup types use a separate upward-step timer.
Ten split low/high addresses for scatter, laser, bounce, flash range, screen flash, invulnerability, energy, power-line ammunition, extra life and diamond rewards, in that subtype order.
High-byte half of the ten collectible reward handlers whose low bytes are at $5B09. The pickup subtype selects the corresponding handler and sound.
Ten effect request values paired with the collectible reward subtypes. The overlap path writes the selected value to the voice-three request byte before dispatching the reward.

Initialize a projectile's shared shape, colour and colour-cycle phase, then test its overlap against the player. Wheel/immunity contact converts it into an explosion; other accepted contact calls the player-damage entry. Advance position by the slot's $CB53/$CB5E velocity bytes, animate its colour, and release it outside the playfield or on nonempty terrain.
Twelve colours indexed by the enemy projectile's phase byte at $CB48+slot.
Eight 64-byte hires sprite records. The three pointer tables at $4FFA-$5002 combine them into TIME OUT!, GAME OVER and CONTINUE? with YES/NO. Rendered directly from these bytes to identify the words.

Seventy-one eight-byte multicolour character components. Messages combine four components per displayed letter. Rendered with shared colours white and grey and per-cell colour black, they form the loading, disk-change and ending labels and level digits.
Continuation of the component font beginning at $5DC8: glyphs 32-63. The loading-screen setup copies this page to $C900.

The final seven component glyphs of the font beginning at $5DC8. The loading-screen setup copies the page beginning here to $CA00, including message and parameter tables after the font's end at $5FFF.
Top 34 character cells for LOADING LEVEL 1-1. The level-digit component entries are patched by $61F3; the bottom row is at $6022.
Mutable world top-left character component in the loading message. $61F3 selects its value from the eleven-level digit-component tables before the message is drawn.
Mutable top-right character component of the loading message's world digit, replaced through $60AB before drawing the message.
Mutable stage top-left character component in the loading message. $61F3 selects its value from the eleven-level digit-component tables before the message is drawn.
Mutable stage top-right character component in the loading message. $61F3 selects its value from the eleven-level digit-component tables before the message is drawn.
Bottom 34 character cells paired with $6000. Four component cells together form each displayed letter or digit.
Mutable world bottom-left character component in the loading message. $61F3 selects its value from the eleven-level digit-component tables before the message is drawn.
Mutable bottom-right world-digit component in the second message row, replaced from $60C1.
Mutable stage bottom-left character component in the loading message. $61F3 selects its value from the eleven-level digit-component tables before the message is drawn.
Mutable stage bottom-right character component in the loading message. $61F3 selects its value from the eleven-level digit-component tables before the message is drawn.
Top 30 component cells for TURN THE DISK !, copied to the loading screen by $6227.
Bottom 30 component cells paired with $6044 to form TURN THE DISK !.
Top 16 component cells for a leading space followed by THE END. $625B appends this to the first eight displayed characters of LOADING LEVEL.
Bottom 16 component cells paired with $6080, forming the ending portion of the loading message.

Eight eleven-entry arrays supply the four component cells of the world digit and the four of its level digit. $61F3 selects a row by the zero-based progression index and patches the loading-message tables.
Eleven world top-right character components, indexed by level number $03EF. $61F3 copies this component into the two-row LOADING LEVEL message before display.
Eleven world bottom-left character components, indexed by level number $03EF. $61F3 copies this component into the two-row LOADING LEVEL message before display.
Eleven world bottom-right character components, indexed by level number $03EF. $61F3 copies this component into the two-row LOADING LEVEL message before display.
Eleven stage top-left character components, indexed by level number $03EF. $61F3 copies this component into the two-row LOADING LEVEL message before display.
Eleven stage top-right character components, indexed by level number $03EF. $61F3 copies this component into the two-row LOADING LEVEL message before display.
Eleven stage bottom-left character components, indexed by level number $03EF. $61F3 copies this component into the two-row LOADING LEVEL message before display.
Eleven stage bottom-right character components, indexed by level number $03EF. $61F3 copies this component into the two-row LOADING LEVEL message before display.
Twelve flags indexed by the level progression. A nonzero value tells $54AE to load an S-prefixed auxiliary file and copy it from the $9000 buffer before loading the level.

Twelve destination high bytes indexed by level. When the corresponding flag at $60F8 is nonzero, the transition copies the auxiliary buffer from $9000 to this page through $FF7F, banking I/O out for the stores.
Fill $CC00-$CF47 and $DAE8-$DBE7 with zero, including overlapping page stores. This clears the terrain screen buffer and lower colour RAM before a level transition.
For 160 cells, take each panel screen byte at $0748, look up its colour in $05C8 and write that colour to $DB48. Screen codes also index the panel's colour table.

Select the $CC00 screen working address, copy three pages beginning at $5DC8 to $C800-$CAFF, select VIC bank $C000 and screen $CC00 with character base $C800, and set the loading display's shared colours. The copy includes the font and the tables following it; the messages use glyph components zero through $46.

Install the loading-band interrupt at $6197 through the hardware IRQ vector, disable CIA1 interrupt sources, enable the VIC raster source and select line $6A. Hide sprites, set the display control and acknowledge pending VIC status before enabling interrupts.

Acknowledge the VIC interrupt and preserve the CPU registers, then write 30 palette entries from $61C7 to both border and background with a timed delay between writes. Return through the resident IRQ exit.

Thirty border/background colour values used by the loading-screen raster handler. Its first and last colours frame the middle band; $61E5 XORs the central twenty-one entries with four to animate them.
Twenty-one animated middle entries of the thirty-colour palette beginning at $61C7. $61E5 toggles their bit two in place; the surrounding entries remain outside that toggle loop.
XOR four into the 21 palette entries beginning at $61CB, changing the loading band's centre colours while leaving its end gradients unchanged.
Index eight eleven-entry component tables with the level index and patch the four quadrants of each displayed level digit in the message rows at $6000/$6022.
Copy the two 30-cell rows at $6044/$6062 into the loading screen at $CD45/$CD6D and set those cells' colour nibbles to eight, selecting multicolour character drawing.
Copy the two 34-cell rows at $6000/$6022 to $CD43/$CD6B and set their colours to eight. Each letter occupies a two-by-two group of component glyphs rather than a byte in an alphabet.
Draw the first 16 cells of each loading-message row and the 16-cell ending rows at $6080/$6090, with colour eight. The resulting two-line character layout reads LOADING THE END.
Nine-byte ASCII-readable driver marker, space DTE space 2.0 space, immediately before the effect-update JMP at $6290.
JMP entry to the resident sound-effect interpreter at $62BC. Gameplay calls this after updating its objects, and the paused path also advances it.
Clear SID registers $D400-$D41B and the parallel effect request/state bytes beginning at $FFC0, then set the master volume to fifteen.
Decrement the current voice's command-duration byte at $6408+X. A negative result resumes pattern decoding at the saved cursor $6409+X; otherwise update its pitch, waveform and pulse streams.
Write $08 to the current voice's control register, clearing gate and holding the oscillator in test, then continue to the next voice or finish according to $03EE.

Interpret pending sound requests for SID voice offsets 14, 7 and 0. Bit seven of a request starts its selected pattern, resetting gate/test state. Pattern flags select envelopes, pitch and waveform streams, pulse modulation and voice-one filter parameters; duration counters retain the command cursor between updates. With $03EE nonzero, return after voice three so the music code can own the other voices.

Read a command flag byte through the current pattern pointer. Bit seven redirects the byte cursor, bit six supplies ADSR bytes, bits five and four install pitch/wave cursors, bit three supplies pulse base and increment, and voice one can take filter settings through bit two. Bit one supplies a duration and continuation cursor; without it the voice request is cleared and silenced.

Advance the voice's pitch stream when enabled. Negative stream commands either jump to another offset or, for $81, set a new frequency high byte. Positive commands supply a duration and signed modular increment; apply that increment to $6406+X and write the result to the SID frequency high register.

Advance the waveform cursor, following its optional offset command and translating its value through $645E into the SID control register. Add the pulse increment to its accumulator with end-around carry and write the same accumulator value to both pulse-width bytes. Finish this voice and, in ordinary gameplay, proceed to the next SID voice.
Add the self-modified filter increment to its accumulator and write that accumulator to $D416. The voice-one pattern filter command replaces both immediate operands.
Immediate accumulator operand at the filter update entry $63FA. Voice-one filter commands set its starting value; successive updates add the separately patched increment and write $D416.

Immediate increment operand in the filter accumulator instruction. A voice-one filter command overwrites it; the following store sends the updated accumulator to SID filter cutoff high register $D416.

Eighteen runtime bytes, arranged in seven-byte voice strides: frequency high byte, frequency increment, command duration and command cursor are addressed here for each SID voice. This is interpreter state initialized by gameplay, not a packed sound pattern.
Command-cursor state at voice offsets zero, seven and fourteen. After reading a duration, the interpreter saves the next pattern offset here for the next command boundary.

Thirty-five split low/high addresses indexed by the seven-bit effect request. Request zero takes the silent path before dereferencing its reserved pointer. The other entries select the resident effect command streams, whose secondary pitch and waveform offsets are relative to the same pattern base.
High-byte half of the thirty-five-entry effect directory beginning at $6418; combine each with the corresponding low byte to locate the selected command stream.

This release includes saved player names alongside the developer records; the final two columns need their menu consumer identified before assigning their meaning.
Voice-one request/state byte. The low seven bits choose an effect pattern and bit seven requests a fresh start; voice two and three use the corresponding byte seven and fourteen addresses later.
Voice-two request/state byte, interpreted at SID register offset seven. The Space power-line path requests pattern ten here; the normal-shot and other events can replace it.
Voice-three request/state byte, interpreted at SID register offset fourteen. It is also the resident effect voice when $03EE leaves voices one and two to music.
Packed-decimal lives counter drawn by $4B5A and changed with decimal-mode arithmetic by the life-loss and life-award entries. The hardware reset vector is not used while the game runs from RAM.
